## Context
Bridge fsck reported unbound Jira issues. ACLI inspection on 2026-08-16 proved the remaining three are not Jira-native work to adopt or archive: each is an exact identity match for an existing local `code_review` artifact, including `rebar-id` label, title, revision, PASS decision, and fingerprint. The missing state is only the forward/reverse binding-store entries.

## Exact mappings
- `a750-2710-e903-4a45` (`firstborn-removable-javalina`) ↔ `REB-806`
- `d494-d34f-cf36-43df` (`festive-egotistic-terrier`) ↔ `REB-807`
- `ee21-fcd3-edad-462c` (`impossible-censorian-kangaroo`) ↔ `REB-808`

## Plan
- Claim this ticket before changing shared tracker state.
- Under `rebar._store.lock.write_lock`, load `BindingStore` and fail closed unless bridge fsck still reports exactly `REB-806`, `REB-807`, and `REB-808` as `unbound_jira`, with no alerting drift or integrity findings outside that set.
- Fail closed unless all three local tickets exist and each Jira issue carries the exact matching `rebar-id` label and artifact identity already verified through ACLI.
- Call the public `BindingStore.bind_confirm` API for each exact pair, atomically `save`, then publish through `commit_and_push_tickets_branch` while retaining the same lock. No ad-hoc tracker git.
- Re-run `rebar bridge fsck --output json`; require empty alerting binding drift and empty store integrity, and re-read each forward/reverse mapping.
- Record before/after evidence on this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `REB-806`, `REB-807`, and `REB-808` map bidirectionally to the three exact existing local code-review tickets listed above.
- [ ] No new local ticket or Jira issue is created, archived, or transitioned.
- [ ] The mutation runs under rebar’s unified tracker write lock and publishes through the supported commit-and-push seam.
- [ ] `rebar bridge fsck` reports no alerting `binding_drift` and no `store_integrity` findings after repair.
- [ ] A ticket comment records the guarded before/after evidence and delivered tracker commit.
